reason: Attention spent on autoplay, badges and hover animation is a screen matter; the person senses what draws the eye.
Paper-tone backgrounds and colour meaning are sensed and read; hex colours are screen wording.
Depth, a single H1 and two equal buttons: sensing hierarchy, reading it, and choosing between competing targets; shadows and modals are screen wording.
Table containers, scrollbars and overflow are about reading and scrolling data on a screen.
Acknowledging an action and not faking success or progress; progress bar and highlight are screen wording (close call for any).
Knowing the workflow is finished and which next step to choose; 'bottom of the current view' is screen wording.
Back button, location hash and an Exit path are about going back and leaving in a browser.
Field labels and contextual help explain what an input is; label wording is screen.
Errors are noticed, read and used to correct course; layout shifts, colours and modals are screen wording.
When validation speaks while a person fills a field; blur, focus and fading messages are screen wording.
Editing text in place and saving on blur; icons, modals and buttons are screen wording.
Reading and scanning events as an agenda rather than a grid; date cells and views are screen wording.
Focus mode limits what can be chosen and gives an exit; pointer events, Esc and header hint are screen wording.
A flow shows where the document sits and clicking a node navigates back; nodes and scrolling are screen wording.
Contrast ratio and scalable text so content can be read; rem/em and colour are screen wording.
Presenting live data and pointing at or highlighting values; cursor, slides and arrow keys are screen wording.
Finding settings by search and a pending-changes bar to confirm saves; menus, toggles and bars are screen wording.
A user list shows who, role and status for quick scanning; avatars and status dots are screen wording.
A pre-ship checklist applied to an interface, not a person doing something with one.
One-click undo after a destructive action, replacing confirmation; toast, dialogs and bottom of screen are screen wording.
Same action same consequence, declared actors and roles; no clearly screen wording beyond 'icon' (close call for visual).
Consent defaults to no and the decline path is as reachable as accept; the solution is medium-free, though 'pre-checked' is a close call for visual.
Back is honoured and navigation keeps its place across screens; navigation position and screens are screen wording.
An agent is a named actor under the same audit and norms; no screen wording.
Wording of refusals and messages must not blame or compare; close call, no screen wording, so any.
Text size and contrast so that reading text stays legible; rem and colour are screen wording.
Leading zeros on numbers read and scanned in headings, lists and columns; headings and columns are screen wording.
Where a badge sits relative to its subject and reading order of a table row; viewport, title and table wording is screen.
Colour in one table column so the eye finds what needs action; colour and columns are screen wording.
A floating assistant must not cover the work the person is looking at; widget, hover and panel are screen wording.
About what a generator ships, the maker of the interface, not a person using one.
Marking referenced data as foreign, with freshness, so the operator can tell it at a glance; table, card, hover and vibes are screen wording.
Every element traces to an intent so none is mistaken for information or a choice; the rule states it holds in every medium.
